## What you are trying to find out

<!-- The question, not the feature. "Was last night worse than usual for this
     time of year?" is more useful than "add a comparison chart" — the tool may
     already answer it a way you haven't found, or the better answer may not be
     the one either of us had in mind. -->

## What you do instead today

<!-- Including "nothing, I gave up" — that is the most useful answer of the
     three. A workaround says what this costs; giving up says what it costs
     and that the cost was too high. -->

## Which decision in DECISIONS.md does this touch, if any?

<!-- DECISIONS.md is short and worth the skim. Several obvious features are
     deliberately absent rather than overlooked:

       D1  no runtime dependencies — anything needing a package is a reversal
       D2  raw µg/m³ is canonical; an index is derived for display, never stored
       D3  a scheduled run, not a resident daemon
       D7  an indoor sensor never speaks for the air outside
       D8  health-relevant wording is decided in Python, never in a page

     A request that reverses one is still worth making. Say which, and what has
     changed about the trade — ARCHITECTURE §2.5a and the bundled Python runtime
     are both reversals that were argued and written down. "I didn't know" is
     also a fine answer; leave this blank and we'll work it out. -->

- Decision it touches:
- What has changed about the trade:

## Who it is for

<!-- Yourself is a complete answer. Which providers you use, and roughly what
     kind of setting (a flat, a valley floor, a school, a rural block) — not an
     address. Several features exist because one person described a situation
     nobody had considered. -->

## What would make it wrong

<!-- The most valuable part, and the one that gets skipped. What would this
     feature say on a fresh install with no history? What would it say if the
     data were missing, stale, or from an instrument that has failed? A feature
     that can only confirm what you already believe isn't checking anything. -->

## Anything else

<!-- Prior art, a screenshot of another tool, a link to the science. If this
     rests on a published finding, RESEARCH.md is where that gets recorded. -->
